color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
frozen ContextSnapshot
holds EVERYTHING - policy numbers,
every Coverage figure

div.style: color: rgb(11, 37, 69) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
may_see_record
is there anybody to show?
= assurance is L1 or better

div.style: color: rgb(51, 51, 51) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
NOTHING RENDERS
no name, no policy, no history.
Not a restriction: at L0 there is
simply nobody to render.

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
may_act_on_policy
may they SAY it and DO it?
= assurance is L2 or better

div.style: color: rgb(74, 47, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
SHOWN, BUT NOT YET USABLE
- policy number IS on screen
- coverage figures ARE on screen
- number carries a standing note:
'(ยังไม่ยืนยันตัวตน — ยังใช้/อ้างอิงกับผู้ติดต่อไม่ได้)'
- verify-identity PREPENDED as action 0
- every playbook step above L1 DROPPED
- opening line asks an OPEN question, no name (D55)
- degraded = LOW_ASSURANCE

div.style: color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
FULL USE
- read the number aloud
- confirm a figure
- change a detail, process a claim
- full playbook

div.style: color: rgb(74, 47, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
agent attests on the call (D42):
Confirmed, or a verified third party (D65)

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
this is a RE-RENDER, not a re-fetch.
The data was already in memory.
No round trip to the bank core.
Assurance moves DOWN this way too.

div.style: color: rgb(92, 26, 19) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
D74 reversed D20 here, and it matters. The old rule hid
the record below L2. But the agent needs the record precisely
SO THAT they can verify the caller — hiding it makes
verification impossible, and showing a bank employee the
record they were routed is internal processing, not
disclosure. So assurance gates what the agent may SAY and DO,
never what they may SEE.

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
GATE AT THE WIRE, SERVER-SIDE
BriefOut is a wire DTO, never CaseBrief.model_dump().
Shipping the domain model and hiding fields in React
is defeated by devtools — and it shipped a real leak (B5, D53).

div.style: color: rgb(11, 37, 69) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
gate the SENTENCE on the identity, not the payload.
After a rejection the frozen snapshot still holds the old
policy, so a summary built from the payload will happily print
a number the structured fields correctly withheld. Both
`may_see` and `may_act_on_policy` come from the IdentityResolution.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
the LLM is not even imported here (D16)
every figure is read from a typed Coverage field,
so there is no code path that could put an
invented number on an insurance screen
